question: During the Raja festival, womanhood is celebrated. In which Indian state is this festival extremely popular?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Raja Festival** is a popular festival celebrated in the Indian state of **Odisha**. It is one of the most well-known festivals in the region.
 
• The festival is dedicated to **womanhood** and specifically celebrates **fertility and menstruation**, which is considered sacred and vital for human life.
 
• It is a **three-day festival** that marks the beginning of the agricultural season and is celebrated with great enthusiasm and traditional fervor.
 
• The term "**Raja**" is derived from the Sanskrit word "**Rajas**," meaning menstruation. It is believed that during this time, Mother Earth undergoes a period of rest and rejuvenation, similar to a menstruating woman.
 
• During this festival, women are treated with respect, and they refrain from cooking or performing household chores as a symbol of rest and rejuvenation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Celebration of Raja Festival:**

 
 
• The festival is celebrated in the **month of June**, coinciding with the arrival of the **monsoon season**.
 
• It is also known as "**Raja Parba**" or "**Mithuna Sankranti**" in Odisha.
 
• During the festival, swings (locally called "**Dolies**") are hung from trees, and women enjoy swinging on them as part of the festivities.
 
• Special dishes such as "**Poda Pitha**" (baked rice cake) and other traditional delicacies are prepared and shared among family members and neighbors.
 
• Women wear new clothes, apply **alatha** (a red dye applied to the feet), and participate in folk songs and dances.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Raja Festival:**
 
 
• The festival signifies the **sacredness of womanhood** and acknowledges the importance of menstruation as a natural process vital for life.
 
• It also marks the **agricultural significance**, as it is believed that Mother Earth menstruates during these three days and prepares herself for the upcoming agricultural season.
 
• The fourth day of the festival is known as "**Vasumati Snana**," when women bathe the grinding stone (symbolizing Mother Earth) with turmeric paste and water.
 
 
 
• **Other Indian States:**
 
 
• **Kerala:** Known for its prominent festivals like **Onam** and **Vishu**. It does not celebrate Raja Festival.
 
• **West Bengal:** Celebrates festivals such as **Durga Puja** and **Poush Mela**, but Raja Festival is not significant in this state.
 
• **Maharashtra:** Famous for **Ganesh Chaturthi** and **Gudi Padwa**, but does not have any cultural or traditional association with Raja Festival.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The Raja Festival is a unique celebration of **femininity** and **nature**, emphasizing the interconnectedness between the two.
 
• It highlights the cultural values and traditions of **Odisha**, making it an integral part of the state's identity.
 
• Through this festival, the community also acknowledges and respects the **biological processes** of women, offering a break from their daily responsibilities.
 
• The festival also brings families and communities together, strengthening **social bonds** through shared traditions and joyful celebrations.
